correctness.rationale: For n invertible in k, the binomial line families are finite-étale and have only the three coordinate pencil vertices plus pairwise intersections. Three-line concurrence is equivalent to u*v*w=1, giving either three disjoint double-point schemes or one triple-point scheme E_a x E_b. Tracking all normalization fibers proves the Grothendieck formula and then each extension count and zeta. The nonstandard example uses irreducible t^3-2 over F7, with Frobenius 3-cycles. The delivered checker directly enumerated all points in 11994 small prime-field parameter cases and F343; those finite tests are corroboration, not the uniform proof.

value.rationale: The classical three-pencil Fermat family gives a natural, complete finite-field descent problem. The scalar-product boundary changes the entire inner incidence scheme from 3n^2 ordinary nodes to n^2 triple points, and the arithmetic formula precisely distinguishes nonrational lines from rational points at their intersections. It determines a full Hasse--Weil invariant across all parameters/degrees and yields an infinite sequence of fields on which a nine-line divisor has only the three coordinate points. Neither an arbitrary numerical slice nor a generic normalization exercise is asserted as the value.
